R1140.summary: Beatrice of Aragon writes to her sister Eleonora, Duchess of Ferrara, during the War of Ferrara: for 100,000 ducats sent to Milan, King Matthias would raise 16,000 men (10,000 Swiss and 6,000 cavalry) in the Brescia and Verona districts against Venice, but will not declare himself openly before his relations with the league are settled. Decryption: uncorrected OCR of the printed decipherment in Magyar Diplomácziai Emlékek III (1877) no. 10.
R1140.en:
Most Illustrious Lady, most honoured Sister, after due recommendation. I am writing more fully on behalf of His Majesty
the King my consort to His Majesty the Lord King our father about the matters below, for fear these letters might
miscarry, the road being dangerous; and I shall leave long words aside and come to the conclusion. Having understood the
danger you are in, the Lord King of Hungary, notwithstanding the great business he has in being at war on two sides, one
against the Turk, the other against the attack that the Emperor with the whole Empire seeks to make on him, has
nevertheless decided on an excellent and necessary expedient for the favour and safety of the whole league.

R1141.summary: Beatrice reports Matthias's displeasure at the league's unwillingness to spend, repeats the Swiss and cavalry offer, asks for money to be sent to Milan and calls for action rather than negotiations that keep 'returning to the beginning' like a ball game. Decryption: uncorrected OCR of MDE III (1877) no. 12.
R1141.en:
Most Illustrious Lady and my most honoured sister. I have understood what Your Ladyship [?writes] [?to] me in your
letter of the 14th of last month, and with great displeasure; all of which I have made known to the Most Serene Lord King
my consort, who has had no less displeasure at it; but in part he lays the blame on the whole league, which, had it been
willing to spend, would have had plenty of help at small cost, and such that it would not only have kept the Venetians from harming
[the league], but would have reduced them to scarcity in defending themselves; and he rightly says that so it usually happens to misers,
who to save a groat lose the ducat.

R1156.summary: King Matthias Corvinus to Duke Ercole I of Ferrara, his brother-in-law, in the first weeks of the War of Ferrara: he and Queen Beatrix had resolved to send 500 picked horse, among them 100 hussars, but found no safe road; his captain Balázs Magyar goes to Croatia towards the Venetian border to gather troops. Printed by Fraknói (1895, no. 131); re-read from the signs and against the clear copy of the time.
R1156.en:
Revised 14 Nov 2026 with the reading (see its note): electos, Regi Hungarie, quod venient, the name signs.

Matthias, by the grace of God King of Hungary, Bohemia etc., to the most illustrious prince, Lord Hercules, Duke of
Ferrara and Modena etc., greeting and success according to his wishes. From the letters of the most illustrious Lady
Duchess, your consort, our dearest sister and sister-in-law, we have learned the state of your affairs and the
preparations of the Venetians against you, which we did not hear gladly; [and] that the most serene lord, our king
and our dearest father, and your other lords and confederates are to help you, and that they have already in fact
begun; we too, out of our singular goodwill towards you, shall not fail to do those things which we know will be of
use to you.

snip.cap: The king’s letter of 1 June 1482: invented-sign runs inside the clear Latin (the 500 horse)
snip.credit: Archivio di Stato di Modena, Cancelleria, Carteggio principi esteri 1622, b. 1/3, no. 2, via DECODE R1156

system: Graphic substitution alphabet with homophones, signs for doubled letters (tt, ss, ff, ll) and name signs. The queen's two letters use few homophones (a, o, u, n) and two name signs (King of Hungary, Venetians); the king's letter uses the same values with more…
